scenes.tts: The first film used ordered arrival to map a chromosome. How can a phage reveal which genes sit close together? Keep following gold donor DNA. The carrier has changed, so the readout must change too.
scenes.caption: The first film used ordered arrival to map a chromosome. How can a phage reveal which genes sit close together? Keep following gold donor DNA. The carrier has changed, so the readout must change too.
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 schematic world and exact COLOUR MAP: donor DNA GOLD; recipient LIGHT GREY; donor TEAL; phage PURPLE; F factor ORANGE; recipient chromosome WHITE; filter BLUE; DNase RED. Begin on the first film's white circular map with moving gold markers. Transform the teal donor connection into several purple phages approaching the same grey recipient. The question appears above them. Keep 'schematic' at bottom right.
scenes.narration: The first film used ordered arrival to map a chromosome. How can a phage reveal which genes sit close together? Keep following gold donor DNA. The carrier has changed, so the readout must change too.

scenes.visual: Title 'When Genes Share a Phage' fades in above the carried chromosome-and-phage world. Purple phages drift and gold marker blocks move around the white chromosome.

scenes.tts: Genes can cross a cell-blocking filter inside phage particles, protected from deoxyribonuclease. In generalized transduction, a phage sometimes packages host DNA instead of phage DNA. Any host region can be sampled. The coat reveals the route; the host fragment creates the mapping signal.
scenes.caption: Genes can cross a cell-blocking filter inside phage particles, protected from DNase. In generalized transduction, a phage sometimes packages host DNA instead of phage DNA. Any host region can be sampled. The coat reveals the route; the host fragment creates the mapping signal.
scenes.visual: A BLUE filter slides in. Purple phages pass through while grey cells stop. A RED DNase sweep leaves the gold cargo intact. Expand one TEAL donor so its WHITE chromosome fills the frame. A purple empty head moves around the chromosome like a sampling window, then encloses one short GOLD host segment. Repeat at different positions without implying equal probability.
scenes.narration: Genes can cross a cell-blocking filter inside phage particles, protected from DNase. In generalized transduction, a phage sometimes packages host DNA instead of phage DNA. Any host region can be sampled. The coat reveals the route; the host fragment creates the mapping signal.

scenes.tts: P twenty two carries host fragments in Salmonella. P one does this in E coli. Each transducing particle delivers only a limited chromosome segment. The phage carries a short window, not the whole circular chromosome.
scenes.caption: P22 carries host fragments in Salmonella. P1 does this in E. coli. Each transducing particle delivers only a limited chromosome segment. The phage carries a short window, not the whole circular chromosome.
scenes.visual: Keep the moving sampling window on the same chromosome. Change the donor label from 'Salmonella: P22' to 'E. coli: P1' while the purple head stays the carrier. The chromosome zooms out, and the gold segment remains visibly short compared with the full white circle. Show no numerical scale.
scenes.narration: P22 carries host fragments in Salmonella. P1 does this in E. coli. Each transducing particle delivers only a limited chromosome segment. The phage carries a short window, not the whole circular chromosome.

scenes.tts: Specialized transduction follows another rule. Lambda inserts at one preferred site between gal and bio. Inaccurate removal can carry only neighbouring host genes. This is not random sampling across the chromosome; attachment site position matters.
scenes.caption: Specialized transduction follows another rule. Lambda inserts at one preferred site between gal and bio. Inaccurate removal can carry only neighbouring host genes. This is not random sampling across the chromosome; attachment-site position matters.
scenes.visual: Transform the moving sampling window into one PURPLE lambda block fixed at a labelled site between WHITE blocks 'gal' and 'bio'. The block lifts out unevenly and takes one adjacent GOLD block. Distant markers stay white. Label this branch 'specialized'; do not mark distant genes impossible by any other route.
scenes.narration: Specialized transduction follows another rule. Lambda inserts at one preferred site between gal and bio. Inaccurate removal can carry only neighbouring host genes. This is not random sampling across the chromosome; attachment-site position matters.

scenes.tts: Return to generalized transduction. Two genes can share one particle only when one host fragment covers both. Closer markers fit together in more possible windows. Move the window and count how often both markers remain inside.
scenes.caption: Return to generalized transduction. Two genes can share one particle only when one host fragment covers both. Closer markers fit together in more possible windows. Move the window and count how often both markers remain inside.
scenes.visual: Restore the large WHITE chromosome arc and a fixed-width PURPLE sampling window. Show one close pair of GOLD marker blocks. Slide the window through several positions that cover both. Then show a wider pair; fewer window positions cover both. Keep all positions schematic and continuously move the window.
scenes.narration: Return to generalized transduction. Two genes can share one particle only when one host fragment covers both. Closer markers fit together in more possible windows. Move the window and count how often both markers remain inside.

scenes.tts: Two marker pairs produce different shared-carriage bars. One bar is high, and one is low. Which pair lies closer on the chromosome? Compare only the bars; do not infer direction yet.
scenes.caption: Two marker pairs produce different shared-carriage bars. One bar is high, and one is low. Which pair lies closer on the chromosome? Compare only the bars; do not infer direction yet.
scenes.visual: Place the close-looking and wider-looking pairs behind neutral covers labelled 'pair A' and 'pair B'. Beside them, grow one tall GOLD bar and one short GOLD bar labelled only 'shared carriage'. Ask 'Which pair is closer?' Do not display numbers or uncover the spacing.
scenes.narration: Two marker pairs produce different shared-carriage bars. One bar is high, and one is low. Which pair lies closer on the chromosome? Compare only the bars; do not infer direction yet.

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Hold the two qualitative bars and covered marker pairs. Purple sampling windows drift slowly behind the bars; reveal nothing.

scenes.tts: The pair with the higher shared-carriage bar is closer. More fragment positions can include both markers, so more particles deliver them together. The bar summarizes many particles, not one specially chosen fragment.
scenes.caption: The pair with the higher shared-carriage bar is closer. More fragment positions can include both markers, so more particles deliver them together. The bar summarizes many particles, not one specially chosen fragment.
scenes.visual: Uncover the marker pairs. The tall bar aligns with the visibly close pair. Animate several purple windows covering both close markers, then only a few covering the wider pair. Keep a small 'schematic' label beside the qualitative bars.
scenes.narration: The pair with the higher shared-carriage bar is closer. More fragment positions can include both markers, so more particles deliver them together. The bar summarizes many particles, not one specially chosen fragment.

scenes.tts: Researchers select recipients that gained one donor marker. Then they score the fraction that also gained another. That fraction is the cotransduction frequency. Selection defines the denominator before the second marker is counted.
scenes.caption: Researchers select recipients that gained one donor marker. Then they score the fraction that also gained another. That fraction is the cotransduction frequency. Selection defines the denominator before the second marker is counted.
scenes.visual: A purple phage injects gold DNA into many grey recipients. A plate first retains only recipients with a GOLD selected-marker badge. Among those colonies, some gain a second BLUE-OUTLINED badge. A bracket gathers that subset into a bar labelled 'cotransduction frequency'. Use no counts or percentages.
scenes.narration: Researchers select recipients that gained one donor marker. Then they score the fraction that also gained another. That fraction is the cotransduction frequency. Selection defines the denominator before the second marker is counted.

scenes.tts: Frequencies against one selected marker rank proximity, but cannot place genes left or right. Three-factor classes settle the order. The same proximity can sit on either side of the selected marker.
scenes.caption: Frequencies against one selected marker rank proximity, but cannot place genes left or right. Three-factor classes settle the order. The same proximity can sit on either side of the selected marker.
scenes.visual: Put one selected GOLD marker in the centre. A second marker appears at equal schematic distance first on the left, then on the right; the same qualitative bar stays unchanged. Add a third marker and transform the line into four plain class cards. Leave their interpretation as a question for the text; show no rarest class or answer.
scenes.narration: Frequencies against one selected marker rank proximity, but cannot place genes left or right. Three-factor classes settle the order. The same proximity can sit on either side of the selected marker.

scenes.tts: Shared carriage is not the whole colony. The donor fragment must enter and be expressed. For stable inheritance, it must also recombine into the recipient chromosome. A colony combines transport, recombination, expression, and survival under selection.
scenes.caption: Shared carriage is not the whole colony. The donor fragment must enter and be expressed. For stable inheritance, it must also recombine into the recipient chromosome. A colony combines transport, recombination, expression, and survival under selection.
scenes.visual: Carry one purple phage and grey recipient forward. Gold DNA enters, briefly sits beside the WHITE chromosome, then aligns with a matching white segment. Two flanking joins replace that segment with gold. Three labels appear in order: 'entry', 'expression', 'stable integration'.
scenes.narration: Shared carriage is not the whole colony. The donor fragment must enter and be expressed. For stable inheritance, it must also recombine into the recipient chromosome. A colony combines transport, recombination, expression, and survival under selection.

scenes.tts: Interrupted mating maps long chromosome stretches by time. Cotransduction resolves a local interval by shared carriage. Each route creates its own map readout. Neither readout gives physical base pairs directly in this lesson.
scenes.caption: Interrupted mating maps long chromosome stretches by time. Cotransduction resolves a local interval by shared carriage. Each route creates its own map readout. Neither readout gives physical base pairs directly in this lesson.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full WHITE chromosome. On the left, the first film's long marker timeline wraps around it. On the right, a PURPLE sampling window magnifies one short interval with qualitative cotransduction bars. Both remain visible and moving while a central arrow reads 'route → readout → map'.
scenes.narration: Interrupted mating maps long chromosome stretches by time. Cotransduction resolves a local interval by shared carriage. Each route creates its own map readout. Neither readout gives physical base pairs directly in this lesson.

scenes.tts: For generalized transduction, shared carriage maps proximity. Closer genes travel together more often, within the phage's limited load. Compare markers under the same phage and experimental conditions.
scenes.caption: For generalized transduction, shared carriage maps proximity. Closer genes travel together more often, within the phage's limited load. Compare markers under the same phage and experimental conditions.
scenes.visual: The purple sampling window slides over a close gold marker pair, and the shared-carriage bar rises. It slides over a wider pair, and the bar falls. Keep 'generalized transduction' and 'schematic' visible.
scenes.narration: For generalized transduction, shared carriage maps proximity. Closer genes travel together more often, within the phage's limited load. Compare markers under the same phage and experimental conditions.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed moving sampling window. Show one centred line only: 'Shared carriage maps proximity; closer genes travel together more often.' Purple phages drift behind it.
